title: Real-World Evaluation of ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA Radioligand Therapy (¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-RLT) as First-Line Treatment for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
summary:
The aim of this study is to investigate the efficacy and tolerability of treatment with the radiolabeled compound ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) when this treatment is used as the first therapy after the development of castration resistance.

For this purpose, existing medical data from patients treated at several specialized centers in Germany will be analyzed. The assessment will include, among other parameters, changes in PSA levels, changes in tumor disease based on imaging examinations, time to disease progression, overall survival, and time to initiation of subsequent systemic treatment. In addition, treatment-related adverse events will be evaluated.

This is a retrospective observational study. This means that no additional examinations or treatments will be performed as part of the study. Only existing data collected during routine clinical care will be analyzed.

The study aims to improve our understanding of the use of ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA radioligand therapy in routine clinical practice and to generate further insights into its efficacy, safety, and clinical relevance for the treatment of patients with mCRPC.

interventions.name:
Patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) receiving ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA radioligand therapy as first-line treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients (≥ 18 years) with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC).
Patients receiving ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA radioligand therapy as first-line treatment for mCRPC.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients with inconsistent or incomplete data or missing follow-up.
